Conformal level from the same guide set
anchor ← candidate with the lower guide NLL
q̂ = (1−α)-quantile of guide scores → region {−log p̂(y|x) ≤ q̂}
active directions B: they move the region boundary
largest-variance direction: left to the cheap completion
A prediction region depends on the posterior mainly through a few
parameter directions that move its boundary; these are generally
not the directions of largest posterior variance. Score gradients
on the guide set find them; rank r follows a spectral-mass rule.
slice MCMC along B: samples a1 … aN (r-dimensional MALA)
projected VI completion carries the remaining directions
r ≪ d directions sampled: 12–15× faster than full HMC
follows every mode, skips low-density gaps
score gradients pick r directions; no MCMC yet
MCMC only where it matters; VI elsewhere
conformal quantile sets the density level
